premise: I poured my late husband's $118,000 nursing pension into buying and restoring a collection of rare antique sewing machines with my stepdaughter, notarizing a 50/50 partnership and a promise to stitch a free heirloom quilt for each of my grandkids; when a textile museum offered $720,000 for the collection, she forged a dissolution, sold the machines, and mailed me a $4,200 'spool' check. I discovered our original agreement folded inside the bobbin case of an 1890s Willcox & Gibbs, voided the sale, and now run 'Stitch of Deceit Quilts,' where she threads machines in a smock that says 'Unraveled Trust' and every quilt label prints her perjury docket number.
